props.text: A FIELD GUIDE TO DEEP TIME

A wall.
An ocean.
500 million
years.
Descend through a canyon wall. Read the landscapes that came before us, one layer at a time.
Stand on the rim. Beneath your feet, pale limestone remembers a shallow tropical sea. Brachiopods rested on its floor while waves sifted lime-rich mud. Today that ancient seabed holds up the sky.
Choose a layer to return to its place in the canyon.

layers.name: Kaibab Limestone
layers.title: Where the sea became sky
layers.story: Stand on the rim. Beneath your feet, pale limestone remembers a shallow tropical sea. Brachiopods rested on its floor while waves sifted lime-rich mud. Today that ancient seabed holds up the sky.
layers.fact: A shell with unequal valves, belonging to an animal very different from a clam.

layers.name: Toroweap Formation
layers.title: A shoreline on the move
layers.story: The sea advances, then retreats. Salt flats dry in the sun; dunes push toward the water. Thin beds of gypsum preserve the repeated rhythm of a coastline that never stayed still.
layers.fact: Evaporating seawater left calcium sulfate crystals between sediment beds.

layers.name: Coconino Sandstone
layers.title: Footprints across a desert
layers.story: A vast dune field once lay here. Tilted lines record sand slipping down dune faces. Small animals crossed the slopes, leaving tracks that survived longer than mountains.
layers.fact: Cross beds record the direction of migrating dunes.

layers.name: Hermit Formation
layers.title: The river leaves a trace
layers.story: Rivers spread fine red silt across a coastal plain. Ferns grew beside slow channels. Iron in the sediment oxidised, giving these slopes their rust colour.
layers.fact: Delicate leaves record a landscape of seasonal streams and vegetation.

layers.name: Supai Group
layers.title: Land and water trade places
layers.story: This place alternated between river delta, coastal dune and shallow sea. Red ledges and softer slopes are a layered archive of environments in motion.
layers.fact: These marine animals are related to sea stars; their segmented stems often fossilise.

layers.name: Redwall Limestone
layers.title: A cliff made of life
layers.story: Warm clear water held corals and crinoids. Their fragments accumulated into a carbonate platform. The rock is grey inside: red minerals washing down stain its face.
layers.fact: A solitary rugose coral, with growth lines from its life in a Paleozoic sea.

layers.name: Temple Butte Formation
layers.title: Channels cut into time
layers.story: Ancient channels cut into older rocks, then filled with sediment. Erosion removes chapters. Geologists read those absences as carefully as the stone.
layers.fact: Magnesium-rich water altered limestone into a rock containing dolomite.

layers.name: Tonto Group
layers.title: The first great shore
layers.story: The ocean moved across a low continent, laying beach sand, offshore mud and limestone. Trilobites walked this seafloor. A coastline half a billion years old is still underfoot.
layers.fact: An extinct marine arthropod whose segmented armour is an icon of early animal life.
